points.text: Marginal novelty: relevance top-k plus DivPrune greedy; prompt-guided pruning already exists
FastV mischaracterised as using final-layer ViT attention
Very thin baselines: only DivPrune; FastV, SparseVLM, VisionZip, PAR, GlimpsePrune absent
Relevance-only baseline is an author-built strawman
Gains over DivPrune negligible or inconsistent across benchmarks
Single runs with no variance or significance; determinism rationale wrong
Table 2 does not support prompt-awareness; no k=0 or random-prompt control
Per-benchmark ratio k tuned on test set, undermining zero-shot claim
Baseline absolute numbers far below published values, suggesting broken evaluation
MMMU 'official test split' has no public labels
ChartQA gain likely answer-parsing artefact; explanation untested
Qwen2.5-VL setup appears suboptimal; DivPrune possibly mis-reproduced
'Retains ~90% accuracy' claim fails in several cases
Relevance cosine computed across unaligned embedding spaces; no evidence scores meaningful
Mean pooling over all prompt tokens dominated by generic tokens; pooling ablation insufficient
Efficiency analysis thin: single latency number, tiny memory sample, no Qwen or FLOPs
ZSPAPrune slower than DivPrune
Only 7B models evaluated
Only single 90% pruning ratio; no accuracy-vs-ratio curves
Video and high-resolution generality hinted but not evaluated
Prompt-dependent pruning prevents KV-cache reuse in multi-turn queries; not discussed
Presentation errors: Qwen architecture description, typos, notation ambiguity
No pseudo-code or complexity analysis
No comparison with methods balancing task relevance and diversity
Needs validation on more models of different parameter scales
Reimplemented task-relevance baselines may be unfairly tuned
Method overly simple; no theoretical justification or complexity discussion
Framework figure too general; does not highlight innovations
No quantitative comparison with strong prompt-aware baselines like GlimpsePrune
Efficiency claims from single model at 90% pruning; savings sources unanalyzed
Heuristic method without formal objective or robustness/failure analysis
Evaluation limited to ~7B VLMs; larger models untested
Adding diversity to relevance-based pruning is incremental novelty
Figure 1 does not convey why diversity helps pruning
Recent token pruning methods (VisionZip, Dynamic-LLaVA, etc.) not discussed or compared
Average pooling over prompt tokens unreasonable given task-irrelevant tokens
Diversity selection may choose useless background tokens; motivation doubtful
